question.text: Scenario: Arjun Malhotra is preparing a PESTLE analysis of an industry he covers. Among the facts he has compiled are the following: the central government is promoting domestic manufacturing in the sector through a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme; the country is a major exporter of the sector's products; rising health consciousness and an ageing population are increasing demand; digital health, telemedicine, and AI-driven research are opening up new opportunities; a binding regulatory order issued by the government caps the prices of essential products in the sector and is enforceable on manufacturers; and the sector faces growing emphasis on green chemistry, sustainable manufacturing, and effluent treatment compliance. Question 4 of 5: A binding regulatory order capping the prices of essential products in the sector, with enforceable compliance obligations on manufacturers, falls under which PESTLE category?

answer.text: Legal — a specific regulatory order with legal force on businesses

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Research Analyst workbook describes Legal factors as the legal architecture and enforcement environment for businesses. A binding regulatory order with enforceable compliance obligations sits within that Legal architecture rather than within high-level policy. The Trap: Political covers policy intent and ideology; once a policy crystallises into a binding regulatory order with legal force, the relevant PESTLE bucket becomes Legal. Economic captures market outcomes (prices, growth, FX) rather than the compliance instrument itself, and Socio-cultural is unrelated. Note: Category labels and DPCO-specific facts stripped from the scenario; the case is now stated as a generic binding regulatory order so the test of Legal-vs-Political reasoning still works without unsupported source claims. Role-specific pro-tip label removed.
